title: A dense normal open in an integral finite-type scheme
statement:
Every integral finite-type scheme over a field has a nonempty
open subscheme
which is normal.

proof.text: Choose a point x of the integral scheme X and an affine open V containing it. Then B = Γ(X,V) is a domain and X.functionField is its fraction field. The map f induces a finite-type k-algebra structure on B. Apply the already proved Algebra.FiniteType.finite_integralClosure with the degree-one extension X.functionField / X.functionField to obtain a finite B-module integral closure.

Apply the proved source-library lemma exists_isInteger_smul_of_finite_integralClosure to obtain b in the non-zero-divisors of B such that b times every integral element of the fraction field belongs to B. Its proof takes a common denominator of finite module generators and extends the property by span induction. The proved source-library criterion isIntegrallyClosed_of_isLocalization_away gives that B[1/b] is integrally closed: if z is integral over B[1/b], some b^n z is integral over B, so b^(n+1) z belongs to B and z belongs to B[1/b]. These are exactly the denominator-clearing steps of the blueprint, already proved in WeilConjectures.Mathlib.RingTheory.DedekindDomain.IntegralClosure.

The generic point lies in V and the germ of b there is nonzero, hence a unit in the function field. It therefore belongs to the principal open W = D(b), so W is nonempty. The affine basic-open localization identifies its ring of sections with B[1/b]. For every y in W the stalk is a localization of this normal domain at the corresponding prime ideal. Apply isIntegrallyClosed_of_isLocalization to conclude that every stalk on W is integrally closed.
